@kpd_wrangler Yes, I did read the changelog before upgrading. Its only relevant entry is “Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812),” which does not indicate that a default, or fitted results, would change.

I have now traced the problem to PR #812. In `LineList.__init__`, the default changed from `wave_frame='air'` to `wave_frame='vacuum'`, with no deprecation warning. Rest wavelengths are therefore interpreted as vacuum by default, while my arc-lamp calibration and input spectra are in air. The vacuum/air wavelength ratio is approximately 1.00028 near 6563 Å, corresponding to about 83 km/s and exactly the systematic redshift decrease of roughly 0.00028 I reported. Using 2.4.3 with the same spectra and config restores the previous values.

I am frustrated that I spent two days following your assurance that this was “almost certainly” my calibration or config, including unnecessarily re-reducing arc lamps for 40 spectra, while the thread was marked solved before the cause had been established. “Works for me” is not a test of this configuration: spectra already using vacuum wavelengths, or radio data where the optical air/vacuum conversion is irrelevant, would not show this offset. @m_okonkwo also reported a small offset on long-slit data after updating, so this is not limited to my spectra.

For anyone else using air-calibrated spectra with 2.5.0, the workaround is to set the frame explicitly:

`LineList(..., wave_frame='air')`

@lumenfit_maint Please reopen this thread. Could the 2.5.0 CHANGES entry be updated to state clearly that PR #812 changed the default `wave_frame` from air to vacuum and can shift fitted redshifts for air-calibrated data? Calling this only a “refactor” is not enough to identify a scientifically significant behavior change. A warning when `wave_frame` is not explicitly set would also help prevent others from silently obtaining shifted results.
